- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment drops below 0.50 and prices show recent downward momentum, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >3% for 3+ consecutive days), consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 60% true, 40% model) for next 5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive days falling >1%), model often lags — adjust forecast to match trend 1–2 days ahead, not 3–5.  
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model may misread sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence in positive sentiment.
